summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) has heated up again after a tense pause: UKMTO reported tankers attacked north of Oman's Khasab on Nov 17 and Nov 20, and a US military official told Reuters that US aircraft struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island on Nov 17. On Saturday, Nov 21, UKMTO reported two tanker incidents near Khasab (a projectile hit on one tanker's stern and another in a tanker's engine room, possibly the same vessel), and Iran's navy said a tanker caught fire after hitting a mine east of the strait. Iran's and Oman's foreign ministers have discussed keeping shipping routes open, with no agreement announced.

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are controlled by the US and its regional partners. Most traffic moves through a shuttle system the US coordinates with Arab partners, with weekly volumes swinging as attacks continue (Al Jazeera).

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: About 11.6 million barrels a day over the seven days to Oct 13, about 68% of the 17.1 million pre-war baseline (Kpler, via Al Jazeera). This is the latest weekly figure found; no newer one had been confirmed by Nov 18.

status.label: The war
status.note: A US military official told Reuters that US fighter aircraft struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island on Nov 17, after earlier limited US strikes there on Nov 2 and Nov 7 and on launchers at Bandar Lengeh and Sirik over Nov 15-16 (Euronews). On Nov 17 Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a US radar system in Bahrain with drones; Bahrain said it intercepted the attacks. Qatar, a mediator, called for restraint; no deal has been signed.

status.label: Brent crude
status.note: Brent settled at US$92.57 a barrel on Friday, Nov 20 (WTI US$83.98 for the expiring December contract, US$83.41 for the most-active January one), after falling to about US$90 earlier in the day; oil posted a third straight weekly decline (EnergyNow; Bloomberg via Rigzone).

updates.text: UKMTO reported a second incident on Saturday, Nov 21: a tanker hit in its engine room by an unidentified projectile 17 nautical miles east of Khasab; it was not clear whether both reports involved the same vessel, and no casualties were reported. Iran's navy said a tanker caught fire after hitting a naval mine in a restricted area east of the strait; Reuters could not verify the Iranian account.
sources: Reuters via ThePrint: UK maritime agency reports two tanker incidents near Oman; Iran says vessel hit mine east of Hormuz
Jerusalem Post: Two tankers hit by unidentified projectiles in Strait of Hormuz off Oman's Khasab within an hour

updates.text: ABC News reported that UKMTO counted 31 attacks in and around the strait in October and about 19 in November as of Nov 18, more per month than in any earlier month of the war; the IMO counts 34 in October and November so far.
sources: ABC News: Strait of Hormuz attacks have increased to highest level since Iran war began

updates.text: Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran is ready to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the United States fulfils its commitments; no agreement has been announced.

UKMTO said a tanker sailing outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was hit on its stern by an unknown projectile about 11 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, on Saturday, Nov 21; no injuries were reported and the environmental impact was not known.
sources: Reuters via Yahoo News: Tanker hit by unknown projectile near Oman's Khasab, UKMTO says
Anadolu Agency: Oil tanker struck by unknown projectile near Oman

updates.text: US Central Command said in an advisory that ships taking Iranian-origin cargo by ship-to-ship transfer from blockaded vessels may be treated as evading the US blockade and may be stopped, boarded, diverted or captured; Iran had not responded directly, Al Jazeera reported on Nov 20.
sources: Al Jazeera: US targets Iran's ship-to-ship transfers

updates.text: Iranian media said a missile hit Qeshm Island, on the northern side of the strait, on Friday, Nov 20; Tasnim said there was no immediate information on damage, Reuters reported.
sources: Arab News (Reuters): Tanker hit in Strait of Hormuz as missile strikes Iran's Qeshm Island

updates.text: UKMTO said an outbound tanker caught fire after being struck by an unknown projectile about 8 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, on Friday, Nov 20, with no casualties or environmental impact reported; Iran's Revolutionary Guards said the tanker hit a mine.
Reuters and CNBC reported that Houthi missiles fired at Riyadh raised supply concerns and lifted oil prices slightly early on Friday; no damage figures were given.
Bloomberg, carried by Insurance Journal and The Japan Times, reported that Iran stepped up attacks on tankers in and near the Strait of Hormuz just as oil prices slid.

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
